subject.title: fix(plugins): rebuild unverifiable managed npm installs

question: When a managed registry plugin is installed but its lock metadata cannot prove integrity, should a failed clean rebuild leave that old tree quarantined and inactive rather than restore it?
rationale: The code can implement either policy, but choosing between availability of an unverifiable existing tree and fail-closed package integrity is a product and security-boundary decision.

options.title: Keep fail-closed quarantine
options.body: Accept that failed reconciliation leaves the unverifiable plugin inactive, with actionable output identifying the quarantine and repair command.

options.title: Add an explicit recovery policy
options.body: Preserve quarantine by default but provide a maintainer-approved Doctor or operator recovery path rather than requiring manual filesystem restoration.

options.title: Preserve current rollback
options.body: Restore the old tree after npm failure, accepting continued execution of an installation whose registry integrity cannot be verified.

recommendation.title: Keep fail-closed quarantine
recommendation.body: Accept that failed reconciliation leaves the unverifiable plugin inactive, with actionable output identifying the quarantine and repair command.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent current-main history most directly connects this contributor to the plugin installer and integrity-sensitive installation boundary changed by the PR.
